dossier.purpose: TypeScript/Hono HTTP proxy that exposes an OpenAI-style /v1 API (chat/completions, completions, embeddings, responses, models, files, batches, images, audio, Anthropic /v1/messages, realtime websocket) and forwards each request to one of 72 registered provider adapters (src/providers/index.ts:78-151). Provider, credentials and routing (single/fallback/loadbalance/conditional, retry, timeout, cache, guardrail hooks) are supplied per request through x-portkey-* headers or an inline x-portkey-config JSON header (src/handlers/handlerUtils.ts:836-1180). This repo has no gateway-side credential store, no auth layer on its own endpoints, and no persistent usage ledger. It runs via npx/bunx, Docker or Cloudflare Workers, and a browser Console at /public/ shows live logs. A case-insensitive whole-tree search finds no Codex, GPT-6, ChatGPT-OAuth, prompt/request-compression or MCP-server code or docs at this revision. The only 'gpt-6' hits are base64 noise in cookbook notebooks.

claims.claim: Route to 250+ LLMs with 1 fast & friendly API
Designed for fast, reliable & secure routing to 1600+ language, vision, audio, and image models; integrate with any language model in under 2 minutes
Blazing fast (<1ms latency) with a tiny footprint (122kb); battle tested with over 10B tokens processed everyday
Quickstart: `npx @portkey-ai/gateway` (needs Node.js and npm); gateway runs on http://localhost:8787/v1 and the Gateway Console on http://localhost:8787/public/
On the Gateway Console you can see all of your local logs in one place
Example 'OpenAI compatible client' is Portkey(provider='openai', Authorization='sk-***'); no base URL is shown. Supported libraries include REST and OpenAI SDKs
Configs in the LLM gateway allow you to create routing rules, add reliability and setup guardrails
Fallbacks: fall back to another provider or model on failed requests; you can specify the errors on which to trigger the fallback
Automatic Retries: automatically retry failed requests up to 5 times, with exponential backoff
Load Balancing: distribute LLM requests across multiple API keys or AI providers with weights
Realtime APIs: call realtime APIs launched by OpenAI through the integrated websockets server
Secure Key Management: use your own keys or generate virtual keys on the fly

Smart caching supports simple and semantic* caching; Usage analytics: monitor request volume, latency, costs and error rates; footnote '*Available in hosted and enterprise versions' (the asterisk is not on Usage analytics)
Portkey Cloud is the 'Recommended' deployment; an enterprise version adds org management, governance and security; 45+ providers listed

cd gateway
npm i
npm run build
node build/start-server.js

readme.telemetry_and_network: No analytics/telemetry SDK or phone-home call found in the server code: src/ has no telemetry/analytics/sentry/posthog code; the OTLP span builder (src/handlers/services/logsService.ts:97-162) has no caller outside tests; src/apm/index.ts:1 is just console. Server egress goes to the selected provider (e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1, src/providers/openai/api.ts:4) or to a custom host from x-portkey-custom-host / custom_host (src/handlers/services/providerContext.ts:96-107). The custom-host SSRF filter trusts localhost/127.0.0.1/::1/host.docker.internal by default and blocks private ranges unless TRUSTED_CUSTOM_HOSTS is set (src/middlewares/requestValidator/index.ts:50-62, 232-340). Conditional calls: GET /v1/models goes to a control plane only if ALBUS_BASEPATH is set and no provider/config header is sent (src/handlers/modelsHandler.ts:15, 37-48). Guardrail plugins call vendor APIs only when configured: the `portkey` plugin posts to https://api.portkey.ai/v1/execute-guardrails (plugins/portkey/globals.ts:5) using conf.json credentials.portkey.apiKey (conf.json:15-19), and default.log posts request context to a configured logURL (plugins/default/log.ts:13-19). Browser side: the Console served at /public/ (node runtime, not headless, not production; src/start-server.ts:21-51) loads Google Tag Manager (GTM-KX3PMNVR) and scripts from unpkg, cdnjs, jsdelivr and buttons.github.io (src/public/index.html:856-867, 872-873, 1142-1143), and stores per-provider form values in browser localStorage (src/public/index.html:1841-1859). No Portkey account is needed to run locally; README recommends Portkey Cloud as a hosted option (README.md:69). Logs are not persisted: log records are broadcast over SSE to open Console tabs (src/middlewares/log/index.ts:8-48; /log/stream at src/start-server.ts:72-135). Redis is optional via REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING (src/index.ts:49-51). npm install runs a postinstall script (patch-package, package.json:41).

entry_points.what: Node server main (shebang; package.json bin -> build/start-server.js; Rollup input). Parses --port/--headless, serves the Console, the /log/stream SSE feed and the /v1/realtime WebSocket, then calls serve() (src/start-server.ts:1-18, 138-149; package.json:80; rollup.config.js:7).
Hono app: middleware plus every /v1 route; also the Cloudflare Workers entry (wrangler.toml:3).
constructConfigFromRequestHeaders, tryTargetsRecursively (single/fallback/loadbalance/conditional) and tryPost (hooks, cache, retry, upstream fetch).
POST/GET/DELETE /v1/responses handler (Responses wire API); calls tryTargetsRecursively with endpoint createModelResponse.
`npm run build-plugins` (package.json:32): generates the checked-in plugins/index.ts from conf.json plugins_enabled (plugins/build.ts:4-43).
node:20-alpine two-stage image; EXPOSE 8787; ENTRYPOINT npm, CMD run start:node (Dockerfile:2, 29, 46-50).

code.architecture: Request path: src/index.ts (Hono) -> middlewares (src/middlewares/requestValidator: header/config/custom-host validation; hooks: per-request HooksManager; cache: in-memory simple cache only when conf.json cache=true; log: SSE broadcast, node only) -> per-endpoint handlers src/handlers/*Handler.ts (unknown /v1/* paths fall through to proxyHandler) -> src/handlers/handlerUtils.ts builds a target tree from x-portkey-* headers or x-portkey-config, applies the routing strategy (src/services/conditionalRouter.ts for conditional) and runs tryPost: before-request hooks, cache lookup, retryHandler.ts, upstream fetch, response/stream mapping (responseHandlers.ts, streamHandler.ts), after-request hooks. src/handlers/services/*.ts hold the request/provider/response/log/cache/hooks context classes. Provider adapters live in src/providers/<name>/{api.ts,chatComplete.ts,...}, are registered in src/providers/index.ts, and src/services/transformToProviderRequest.ts maps the OpenAI-shaped body to each provider using a field whitelist per endpoint. Guardrail plugins: plugins/<vendor>/manifest.json plus handlers, aggregated into plugins/index.ts. Console UI: src/public/index.html. Cache backends: src/shared/services/cache (memory/file/redis/cloudflareKV).

claim_checks.evidence: Code registers 72 provider adapters (src/providers/index.ts:78-151) and VALID_PROVIDERS lists 74 names including 'portkey' (src/globals.ts:117-192). The docs give inconsistent figures (README 250+/45+/1600+ models; docs/deploy-on-replit.md:5 says 100+). Model counts cannot be derived from code.

claim_checks.claim: Works as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for OpenAI SDKs and other OpenAI-compatible clients (README.md:87, 106)
claim_checks.evidence: Routes exist for chat, completions, embeddings and responses (src/index.ts:147-253). The requested model and reasoning settings pass through: chat `reasoning_effort` (src/providers/openai/chatComplete.ts:118-120) and Responses `model` plus the whole `reasoning` object (src/providers/open-ai-base/createModelResponse.ts:53-56, 97-100). Caveats: only whitelisted fields are forwarded and the other top-level fields are dropped (src/services/transformToProviderRequest.ts:83-124); chat `model` defaults to gpt-3.5-turbo when omitted (chatComplete.ts:13-17); config `override_params` overwrites body fields (src/handlers/services/requestContext.ts:51-60); every request must carry x-portkey-provider or x-portkey-config (requestValidator/index.ts:106-124). Responses support is defined for openai, azure-openai and iointelligence only (src/providers/{openai,azure-openai,iointelligence}/index.ts).

claim_checks.claim: Load Balancing across multiple API keys or providers with weights (README.md:175)
claim_checks.evidence: strategy.mode 'loadbalance' picks one target per request by weighted Math.random(); default weight is 1 and weight 0 is never picked (src/handlers/handlerUtils.ts:693-723). Each target can carry its own provider + api_key (src/middlewares/requestValidator/schema/config.ts:39-47, 78); the cookbook says same-provider accounts can be added (cookbook/getting-started/resilient-loadbalancing-with-failure-mitigating-fallbacks.md:195). Keys come from the client's x-portkey-config header (handlerUtils.ts:1026-1146). There is no sticky-session, health or quota logic, and a failed pick is not retried on another target unless wrapped in a fallback strategy.

handlerUtils.ts:663-691 tries targets in order and stops when the status is not in strategy.on_status_codes (or the response is ok when unset) or when a gateway-exception header is set; schema at config.ts:13-27.

claim_checks.claim: Automatic Retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff (README.md:174)
claim_checks.evidence: Retry exists via async-retry (src/handlers/retryHandler.ts:87-181) with default statuses 429/500/502/503/504 (src/globals.ts:38), but attempts default to 0 unless configured (src/handlers/services/requestContext.ts:148-156). The 5-cap constant MAX_RETRIES is never referenced (src/globals.ts:39) and the schema accepts any number (config.ts:66-75). Backoff is the library default with randomize:false (retryHandler.ts:174-180). docs/deploy-on-replit.md:15 says retries 'come by default', which the code contradicts.

claim_checks.claim: Gateway Console shows all local logs in one place (README.md:114)
claim_checks.evidence: Logs are SSE-broadcast only to currently connected Console tabs (src/middlewares/log/index.ts:8-48; src/start-server.ts:72-135) and the browser table keeps the latest 100 rows (src/public/index.html:2001-2004). Nothing is persisted server-side, streamed responses are recorded only as 'The response was a stream.' (log/index.ts:60-62), and the Console exists only on node when not headless and not production (start-server.ts:21-51).

claim_checks.claim: Usage analytics: request volume, latency, costs and error rates (README.md:188)
claim_checks.evidence: No code in this repo aggregates tokens, cost or error rates. Searching src/handlers, middlewares, services and shared finds only a pass-through modelPricingConfig from an external preRequestValidator that is never set here (src/handlers/handlerUtils.ts:411-416; src/handlers/services/preRequestValidatorService.ts:12-33). The Console log shows only time, method, endpoint, status, duration plus raw request/response JSON (src/public/index.html:1980-2039). README.md:197 marks only some features as hosted/enterprise; this one has no asterisk.

claim_checks.claim: Secure Key Management: own keys or generated virtual keys (README.md:182)
claim_checks.evidence: Own keys work via Authorization / api_key per request (handlerUtils.ts:1148-1150). Virtual keys have no implementation here: virtualKey appears only in types and the models handler (src/types/requestBody.ts:49, 192; src/handlers/modelsHandler.ts:32-35). The conf.example.json integrations and rate_limits (conf.example.json:20-47) are read only by initializeSettings.ts, which no file imports.

claim_checks.claim: Quickstart: `npx @portkey-ai/gateway` serves http://localhost:8787/v1 with the Console at /public/ (README.md:59-65)
claim_checks.evidence: bin -> build/start-server.js (package.json:80); default port 8787 (src/start-server.ts:13-16); /public/ route registered when not headless/production (start-server.ts:21-51); /v1 routes at src/index.ts:103-295.

No benchmark harness or results in the repo; the only benchmark script is a LogsService micro-benchmark (tests/unit/src/handlers/services/benchmark.ts:58-64, 94-157) and no build output is present. docs/deploy-on-replit.md:12, 17 give different figures (9.9x faster, ~45kb, 100B tokens).

benchmarks.value: '<1ms latency' (README); '9.9x faster' (Replit doc); no methodology or harness published
over 10B tokens everyday (README) vs over 100B tokens (Replit doc)

risks: Scope vs the stated need: no Codex or GPT-6 handling or docs exist anywhere in the tree. OpenAI auth is only a static `Authorization: Bearer <api key>` plus optional OpenAI-Organization/Project/Beta headers (src/providers/openai/api.ts:5-27), so there is no ChatGPT/OAuth/session-token account support; OAuth code exists only for Vertex and Azure (src/providers/google-vertex-ai/utils.ts:115-152; src/providers/azure-openai/utils.ts:13-37). Features the README lists, such as virtual keys, budgets, semantic cache, RBAC and usage analytics, have hooks but no implementation in this repo and sit beside hosted/enterprise offerings (README.md:149-163, 182-189, 197, 265-275).

Pooling semantics are minimal: 'pooling' means a client-supplied list of api_key targets in an x-portkey-config header, picked by weighted Math.random() per request with no affinity, quota or health tracking (src/handlers/handlerUtils.ts:693-723, 1026-1146). Failover happens only through a fallback strategy on status codes (handlerUtils.ts:663-691); retries default to 0 (src/handlers/services/requestContext.ts:148-156) and MAX_RETRIES is unused (src/globals.ts:39). The circuit-breaker and pre-request-validator hooks are read from the Hono context but never set in this repo (handlerUtils.ts:646-658, 793-799; src/handlers/services/preRequestValidatorService.ts:12-20), and initializeSettings.ts (conf.json integrations/rate limits) is imported by nothing.

Usage recording is transient and incomplete: logs go only to open Console tabs (src/middlewares/log/index.ts:8-48), the browser keeps 100 rows (src/public/index.html:2001-2004), and streamed responses are logged as 'The response was a stream.' (log/index.ts:60-62). Streamed /v1/responses events are passed through unparsed with no usage extraction (src/handlers/streamHandler.ts:200-201), and no code computes token or cost totals. Hooks, including the default.log plugin, are skipped for createModelResponse because shouldSkipHook allows only chatComplete, complete, embed and messages (src/middlewares/hooks/index.ts:452-454). The Console exists only on node when not headless/production (src/start-server.ts:21-51).

Responses-API fidelity: the body is rebuilt from a fixed whitelist of 29 fields (src/providers/open-ai-base/createModelResponse.ts:40-157; src/services/transformToProviderRequest.ts:83-124), so any other top-level field a client sends is dropped. On non-proxy routes only provider-mapped headers (Authorization, OpenAI-Organization, OpenAI-Project, OpenAI-Beta) plus configured forward_headers go upstream (src/handlers/handlerUtils.ts:114-139; src/providers/openai/api.ts:5-27). The handler reads the body with c.req.json() (src/handlers/modelResponsesHandler.ts:15) and no code decodes compressed request bodies (no content-encoding handling in src/ beyond deleting response headers, src/handlers/services/responseService.ts:127-130), so compressed request bodies are not handled (inferred from the code, not executed). WebSocket upgrade exists only for /v1/realtime (src/start-server.ts:138-144). The gateway has no request-compression feature at all; the only compress() use is hono response compression, skipped on node/workerd/lagon (src/index.ts:57-63).

Credential exposure and network surface: provider keys travel in request headers or the inline config (handlerUtils.ts:1026-1035, 1148-1150). By code reading, the log objects carry providerOptions (including apiKey) and the upstream request headers (src/handlers/services/logsService.ts:224-228, 258-263), and the full objects are broadcast over SSE (src/middlewares/log/index.ts:75-84) from /log/stream, which has no authentication (src/start-server.ts:72-135). There is no auth or CORS middleware anywhere in src/ (src/index.ts), and serve() is called with no hostname (start-server.ts:146-149), so exposure depends on Node's default bind (not verified; node_modules is absent). The Console page loads Google Tag Manager and four third-party CDNs in the browser (src/public/index.html:856-867, 1142-1143).

Release and CI hygiene: npm publish has no provenance and the Docker image has no signing or SBOM steps, and `latest` is re-pushed on every release (.github/workflows/npm_publish.yml:18-21; docker_publish.yml:32-44). The only test workflow is comment-triggered ('run tests', no author check) with production-environment secrets and runs a nonexistent script `npm run build/start-server.js` (run_tests.yml:9-11, 28, 73-75; package.json:25-42). No workflow runs plugin tests, no tests cover /v1/responses, and most provider tests are live-API tests skipped without keys (src/tests/common.test.ts:9-12). Docs have drifted: CLAUDE.md:84 and 90 cite src/handlers/__tests__/ and conf_sample.json, which do not exist; CONTRIBUTING.md:28 cites `make format; make lint` with no Makefile; the README license badge points at Ileriayo/markdown-badges (README.md:16).

Packaging nuance: the opt-in Retry-After path (retryHandler.ts:88, 108-152) relies on a third callback argument that exists only through the repo's async-retry patch (patches/async-retry+1.3.3.patch:9-10), applied via the postinstall patch-package script (package.json:41), and patches/ is not in the npm `files` whitelist (package.json:18-24). npx installs may therefore run an unpatched async-retry (inferred, not executed). The postinstall lifecycle script also runs on consumer installs.

Maintenance visibility: the clone is shallow (one commit, tag v1.15.2), so release cadence and issue/PR history cannot be assessed from it. The package declares no Node engines range (package.json) while the Dockerfile and CI use Node 20. The SECURITY.md support table covers '1.x.x' only (.github/SECURITY.md:5-7).
